P1: The search returned 120 refunds, all to cards issued in one country. But it is unclear whether the search covered all of M's refunds. It could have been limited, for example by a filter or a cap. The text says "a search of M's refunds over the past 30 days returned 120 refunds," which suggests it returned the refunds M made, but it does not say the search was complete. Taken at face value, the search of M's refunds returned all refunds to one country, so M sent none to other countries. But a search can be incomplete, and the text doesn't say whether it was. Also, refunds rose in the past week, so 120 may be plausible for 30 days. The answer is probably "Cannot tell" because completeness is unknown. The question tests whether we assume the search is exhaustive. I'll go with Cannot tell.

P2: The link took effect at 09:40 and the check scored at 10:00, so the link was in effect before scoring. Whether the check had access to that link is unknown, since data may lag. "Available to it" is not established. Cannot tell.

P3: A rise from 1 to 6 percent is a sixfold increase, and the question is whether it warrants review. Review is a reasonable response to a sharp, unexplained change, and the linkage to a closed account adds to it. Yes.

RESULT PN-003 | P1: Cannot tell | P2: Cannot tell | P3: Yes
